reports.title: STAR BULK CARRIERS CORP. REPORTS NET PROFIT OF $141.9 MILLION FOR THE THIRD QUARTER OF 2026,

desk.headline: Revenue up 39% to $366.9m and adjusted EPS $1.28, both beat; dividend raised to $1.00; no formal guidance
results: Voyage revenue rose 39% to $366.9m, well above the $307.1m estimate, even with a smaller average fleet (134.8 ships vs 141.4).
Higher charter rates did the work: the fleet earned $24,616 a day vs $16,634 a year ago, with Capesizes at $35,713 a day.
Net income jumped to $141.9m from $18.5m; adjusted EPS of $1.28 edged past the $1.265 estimate.
Dividend raised to $1.00 a share (the 23rd in a row, highest since Q3 2022), payable 11 December to holders on 1 December.
A September Athens listing raised $124.4m; the eight-ship Kamsarmax newbuild programme finished in November, and cash was $766m against $1.04bn of debt.

guidance.summary: Star Bulk gives no formal financial guidance. The CEO said the company is constructive on the dry bulk market into year-end, citing longer trade routes, port congestion and seasonal strength.

watch: Q4 charter rates and booked days, likely detailed on the 19 November call.
How the $766m cash pile is used: fleet growth, buybacks or dividends under the full-payout policy.
Trade risks the company flags, including US–China port fees and disruption around Hormuz and the Red Sea.
